This Appeal, Coming On For Hearing, This Day, The
Court Delivered The Following:
 Judgment

The present appeal is filed by the appellant- Insurance Company challenging the judgment and award dated 15.04.2015 in MVC.No.1368/2013 by the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Bangalore (SCCH-11), questioning the liability on the ground that the driver of the motor vehicle bearing No.KA-01-EX-2068 was not holding driving licence to drive the motor cycle as on the date of the accident.
2. The accident was caused on 26.01.2013.
It was specifically contended by the Insurance Company before the Tribunal that the driver of the motor cycle was not holding driving licence as on the date of the accident.

When such contention is raised by the Insurance Company, then it is the burden on the owner of the motor cycle or driver of the motor cycle to produce the driving licence, but they have not produced before the Tribunal.
Therefore, it is proved that the driver of the motor cycle was not holding driving licence as on the date of the accident to drive the motor cycle.

sentences.text: Ex.R.6 is the driving licence extract, but the driver obtained the driving licence after the date of the accident on 26.01.2013.
Therefore, it is proved that as on the date of the accident, the driver was not holding driving licence to drive the motor cycle.
Therefore, the Insurance Company is not liable to pay the compensation.

4. However, in view of Sub-section 2 of Section 147 of MV Act, if the Insurance Company is able to establish its defence, but the fact that the claimant is a third party, then the Insurance Company has to satisfy the claim at the first instance to the claimant and then recover it from the owner of the motor cycle bearing No.KA-01-EX- 2068 as per Sub-sections (1), (4), (7) of Section 149 of the MV Act and also as per the principles of law laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the cases of National Insurance Company Limited Vs. Swaran Singh And Others 1, Pappu And Others -V- Vinod Kumar Lamba and Another2 and New India Assurance Company Limited vs. Yellavva And Another 3.

sentences.text: Therefore, an order of pay and recovery is made.
Accordingly, I proceed to pass the following ORDER I.
Appeal is allowed-in-part.
II. The impugned judgment and award dated 15.04.2015 in MVC.No.1368/2013 by the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Bangalore (SCCH-11), is modified.

III. The appellant-Insurance Company shall satisfy the compensation to the claimant at the first instance, since the claimant is a third party and then recover it from the owner of the motor cycle bearing No.KA-01-EX-2068.
 IV.
No order as to costs.
V. Registry is directed to transmit the TCR along with copy of this order to the Tribunal forthwith.
VI. The amount in deposit made by the Insurance Company shall be transmitted to the Tribunal forthwith.
